title: Assistive overhaul: implemented candidate
summary: Candidate codeArbiter: agreed spec, maintained plan, useful implementation, actual checks and honest DONE; no duplicate permission ceremony. Authorized context population and refresh now use bounded inspection, optional agents and exact native preview/apply without per-document approval receipts. Source bindings describe implementation, not semantic verification or host qualification. The October 7 diagram layout is a historical visual reference, not the current executable workflow. One installed Claude model journey passed before this context extension; Codex and Pi live model cells remain unverified. Final-head package confirmation and release qualification remain incomplete. No release or all-host qualification is implied.

changes.summary: Routine artifact instructions now focus on the installed writer, typed plan, bounded task reads, factual prerequisites, actual checks and safe retry. The default leaf is about 7.3 KB and includes an executable stdin bootstrap with optional operation-schema discovery; explicit attestation remains available on demand without burdening ordinary task context.

Plan authoring preserves agreed criteria, useful tasks, real dependencies and bounded shared inputs. It maintains structurally valid drafts without separate user approval codes or repetitive historical workflow guidance.

The pinned native bridge enables task-context as a bounded informational read and does not require future reviewer/approval producers simply to author a structurally valid draft. Context requests route to ordinary context-preview, context-finalize-preview and exact-reference context-apply; historical receipt input stays a separate compatibility path. Installed host qualification is separate. Native Pi writer admission does not establish a complete live Pi workflow.

A new explicit batch review can select a passing rerun of still-reviewed work without replacing the original task review. The selected run must match its own recorded workspace; changed source or supporting evidence still requires reassessment.

The user-facing route table points feature and sprint work at useful planned execution and selected context refresh at its existing owner. Existing authorization covers ordinary work; actual host, destructive-action and commit controls remain.

The skill index labels planning, execution and optional reviewers as assistive. Context creation uses bounded inspection with optional agents; selected refresh reuses existing authorization instead of a repeated per-document approval stage.
The sprint caller performs an index-first recorded-intent read, preserves actual owner decisions and ADR conflicts, then proceeds with authorized work without a second artifact approval system.
The sprint entry now routes to the assistive implementation body instead of requiring a fresh user approval and two reviews per task.
The feature entry now resumes a maintained spec/plan and task progress without another artifact certification prompt; independent commit and test controls remain.
Source refinement respects recorded deferrals and accepted ADR conflicts without turning each ordinary method adjustment into a separate authorization interview.
Attended feature execution now treats checkpoints as progress groups, not compulsory approval stops; it forwards real failures and continues independent work.

Execution reads one bounded task, does relevant work, rechecks affected inputs and records observed outcomes. No compulsory reviewer chain or receipt-driven restarts; genuine host/security controls and user stops still apply.

TDD uses the authoritative selected spec, exact criterion IDs and plan binding. Matching an agreed criterion needs no additional artifact approval or reviewer; only material outcome changes or real security/host decisions escalate to their owner. A planned command or reported UNKNOWN is never fabricated passing evidence.
The commit owner retains actual user commit permission, staged diff inspection, secrets and focused tests without requiring an artifact-specific acceptance receipt to stage.
PR preparation now reports unfinished implementation and verification honestly while retaining Git, merge ancestry and exact-head hosted CI controls.

Read-only task-context includes complete selected criteria and relevant constraints, names omitted source and intent references, and reports scoped_changed, scoped_unchanged or unassessed without claiming full dependency coverage.

An unanswered legacy reconciliation can be superseded only when route and pending state agree and no durable attempt or matching observed reply exists. Captured replies recover through their original immutable source and receipt; in-flight mutations retain exact replay and real user stops.
The installed recover command finishes a captured original reply or replays an in-flight mutation without asking for a new user answer.

Task-check observations now retain directly referenced criterion identity and an optional bounded source-input fingerprint or an explicit unassessed reason, without executing tests or minting approval receipts.

New checks bind the selected criterion and applicable constraint bodies, including explicit references and scope applicability. Unrelated constraints remain outside the digest; old observations never gain unassessed constraint coverage.
Exact and batch symbol retrieval exposes reported check history under existing response budgets, without a snapshot or approval ticket.
Human HTML presents reported command checks in an escaped, explicitly unverified section; implementation state and source validation remain distinct.

The closed task-check request accepts bounded command observations matched to plan definitions. Ordinary context-preview and context-finalize-preview omit prompt identity; context-apply accepts an exact preview reference and digest. Invalid requests, changed preimages and stale CAS writes remain rejected.
The unpublished 0.3.2 native schema adds optional shared_inputs and scoped task-check fields without silently relabeling old records.

The bounded source-fingerprint reader hashes actual declared task/shared paths, directory membership and known build-control files; unsafe, missing and over-limit scopes are explicitly unassessed rather than blocking work or proving a full dependency graph.

The candidate-only runbook distinguishes 0.3.1/0.3.2 mixed-schema readers, exact replay and forward recovery while preserving recorded user stops. The paired prompt retirement scans immutable observed replies before calling a request unanswered; submitted or uncertain decisions are never erased. Older-client downgrade after modern edits remains unsupported.

The existing paired approval adapter can retire a genuinely unanswered 0.2 sprint-pair request using its serialized cancellation lock and submission check; a submitted decision must replay, while old standalone approval 0.1 intentionally refuses automatic retirement.

The existing prerequisite adapter can retire only a validated ARMED pending question under its original per-plan OS lock. Confirmed or captured decisions are not disposable; no authority receipt or new native permission API is created.

The old paired approval producer publishes a content-addressed observed reply before its durable submission. Cancellation checks the matching observation, content hash, prompt and frozen context under its existing lock, with a strict scan bound. A matching or uncertain pre-submission reply blocks automatic retirement; normal tasks and context reads have no added cost.

The optional reference retains the strict historical evidence inputs without replacing the original task review, including paired approval, captured decisions and in-flight recovery. Its verify command requires literal absolute paths; linked agent subdirectories remain unsupported for strict authority review. These limitations apply to requested attestation, not ordinary task start.
The command catalog starts from the agreed outcome and maintained plan; SMARTS is useful for difficult tradeoffs and does not authorize a changed outcome.
Resident instructions preserve existing work authorization and actual owner decisions without another spec approval or a SMARTS record for every routine step.
Status separates reported DONE from independently ACCEPTED work, shows actual blocked decisions, and does not infer an approval request from draft governance state.
Authors derive tests from agreed criteria; routine work does not wait for a separate approval artifact.

Codex dispatch requires attestation only for explicitly claimed host proof; an unavailable requested farm backend is reported without silently switching provider or model. Ordinary context inspection can proceed inline within actual host permissions; an agent label supplies no containment or semantic verification.
Historical sprint approval and SMARTS proof instructions remain available only for existing explicit attestation, outside the ordinary execution path.
The public Codex farm boundary matches its caller: report the unavailable backend and use another provider or model only within existing authorization.

The context preparation helper reads a bounded UTF-8 draft and explicit source files, selects the whole named document and binds exact existing document/provenance bytes. It chooses create, missing-or-v1 adopt, or v2 update; claims remain semantically unreviewed and malformed provenance is preserved for inspection.

The installed --context-draft/--document/--source command prepares a native preview; --context-apply with --preview-sha256 applies that exact reference. Preview retention does not write the content pair. These context modes avoid the scaffolder and do not reset initialized repositories.

Ordinary context-preview retains an inert proposal and exact preimages without approval or review claims. context-apply revalidates the digest, closed request and preview binding before the native paired transaction; context-finalize-preview uses the same exact-reference path for initial population. No approve-context reply is required.

The finite context contract permits a whole-document Markdown entry only as the sole entry for one of five named content targets. Explicit typed field entries remain available; the writer does not expose arbitrary repository-file writes.

Whole-document replacement requires the explicit document selection and exact existing bytes. It preserves CONTEXT frontmatter and initialization state, checks the named document identity and Markdown structure, and retains the code-map size limit. Human content outside the authorized change remains the caller's preservation obligation.

Ordinary create/adopt/update preserves the same source-evidence, selection and compare-and-swap checks as the native transaction. Missing or matching v1 provenance can be adopted; existing v2 ownership can transition through explicit whole-document selection. Original document/provenance preimages remain in transaction history for exact recovery.

Initial finalization binds thirteen output identities, rechecks supporting source evidence, and changes the initialization marker with its paired provenance digest. Ordinary finalization requires no artifact approval receipt and does not certify semantic correctness. Already initialized repositories refuse a new finalization.

The context schema describes both finite field entries and the explicit whole-document entry for the five supported content documents. Its typed structure records evidence references; schema validity does not establish that the claims were independently reviewed.

Brownfield population covers six logical categories and five content documents through direct bounded inspection or optional scoped agents. A qualified scout profile and per-document approve-context receipts are no longer routine prerequisites. Actual host permissions, source-bound unknowns, material owner decisions, protected content and initial-only finalization remain.

A drift audit stays read-only; an already authorized selected or full refresh proceeds without asking again per document. The installed draft/preview/apply example preserves source bindings and selected content. Matching hashes establish identity only; initialized refresh never reruns scaffolding, clears the marker or repeats finalization.

Initial brownfield setup checks the intended repository and actual host permissions, then uses bounded inspection and the installed safe context writer. Ordinary Windows work needs no special scout profile or per-document artifact approval. An existing initialized repository routes to selected refresh instead of another scaffold or population cycle.

Optional context scouts report only their assigned scope, source identities, coverage, conflicts and unknowns. Six logical categories do not require six child agents. A role label or read-only instruction proves neither sandbox containment nor independent semantic verification; actual host permissions and excluded paths still apply.

Release preparation inserts a new version below the entire Unreleased section and above prior versions, preserving pending notes. This guidance correction does not grant publication authority or replace the existing release-PR and hosted qualification boundaries.

The lazy reference map routes provenance drift or requested initialized refresh to context-check after reading selected documents, provenance and the code map. The owner reuses selected scope and existing authorization.
